text: **thm-0047-one-way-nominal-separation** — `25ed5ae34fe7d2d0` (high). Statement: "The verification products are distinct nominal types. The API provides no conversion, `Deref`, or field projection from a weaker verification product to a stronger one; projections from stronger products to weaker products are permitted." Scope: "This is a one-way nominal-separation claim, not an unconstructibility claim. The request products `CryptographicFloorVerifiedRequest` and `VerifiedMcpRequest` retain public fields, so values can be assembled by hand. Possession provenance is addressed separately by THM-0051." Supersedes owner-signature:thm-0047-nominal-separation-wording (sha256 494bbdb5…, Ruling 13), whose wording was demonstrated false at its approval baseline and on the current implementation.

text: **evidence-handle-role-typing-and-seal (ASM-0046 extension)** — `e49adade71f89aba`, `b86c0b8db458d2f3`, `cb13714af5b537bb`, `486eebcd7b8d2584`. APPROVED: proceed with the seal. Add the new per-role evidence types to ASM-0046's opaque-type list, because Verus cannot inspect their private fields once sealed. Record the exact ASM-0046 change and re-sign the affected authority surfaces.

authority: OWNER-RULINGS.md Ruling 17 (the two remaining F1 seals)
text: **http-request-evidence-block-seal, alternative B** — `0f0dc26c60f6d5be`. Do not seal the request evidence block if doing so requires replacing the existing continuation proof with a getter assumption; keep the fields public, as with VerifiedMcpRequest under CF-007. Fix the defect at the signing boundary: sign_request_full and sign_delegated_response_full validate the request evidence block before signing; signing refuses any structurally invalid or continuation-inconsistent block; regression tests show bypassing or corrupting the continuation state is refused before signature creation. Rationale: a proved continuation postcondition is stronger than a structural seal whose proof would depend on a new getter assumption. Do not add a new getter assumption merely to obtain a sealed type. Document that the block intentionally retains public fields and that its boundary is validation at every signing entry point; include every other signing entry point that accepts the same block in the validation census. Supersedes the seal-and-delete-validate() text of owner-signature:http-request-evidence-block-seal.
